entries.proposition: System: avian DT40 bursal lymphoblast cells, an 80 kb deletion of PRKN intron 7 made by CRISPR with a floxed blasticidin template; not human, not neural.
entries.snippet: we deleted 80 kb of intron 7 in PRKN in our model system, the avian cell line DT40

entries.proposition: PRKN expression is reported unchanged by the deletion at protein reporter and mRNA level.
entries.snippet: No change in either PRKN2YFP transcript levels (Figure 2B) or total PRKN transcript levels (Figure 2C) were detected in any of the clones

entries.proposition: Text: parkin-2YFP levels are similar in the deleted and parental lines.
entries.snippet: The levels of parkin-2YFP were similar in the intron 7-deleted clone and the parental cell line.

experimental_context.comparator: full-length PRKN, parental and heterozygous internal control

entries.proposition: Fragility result: deleting about 12 percent of the gene gives about 50 percent less breakage.
entries.snippet: Notably, the deletion, which is equivalent to approximately 12% of the length of PRKN, resulted in an approximately 50% reduction of the fragility of the gene.

experimental_context.comparator: full-length PRKN, parental and heterozygous internal control

entries.proposition: Figure 3C: after aphidicolin, breakage or constriction of the full-length allele is about 19 percent (parent, n = 270 alleles), 16 percent (clone 18, n = 171) and 18 percent (clone 29, n = 167) against about 8 and 10 percent for the deleted allele of the same cells, with P = 0.032 and 0.011 by Fisher exact test and n for the two alleles identical within each clone (paired alleles from the same spreads); DMSO baselines about 0.5 to 1.5 percent.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 3C: bar chart breakage/constriction (percent of spreads) for DMSO (blue) and APH (red) in P2Y-TT full-length, and clone 18 and clone 29 full-length and delta-intron7 alleles, with n under each bar (210/270, 135/171, 121/167) and P values above the brackets.

entries.proposition: Karyotype caveat: two of fourteen clones from the targeting were trisomic for chromosome 3, read by the authors as a risk of mis-segregation when targeting PRKN.
entries.snippet: This suggests that there is a high risk of chromosome mis-segregation associated with targeting of the PRKN gene.

entries.proposition: Supplementary Figure 2F: of the screened clones plotted, two (clones 5 and 13) are largely or wholly chromosome 3 trisomic and the rest diploid; the screened set is the 14 clones the text counts.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Supplementary Figure 2F: stacked bar chart % of spreads with chromosome 3 trisomy (orange) or diploidy (green) per clone; most clones are 100 percent diploid; two clones show orange bars.

entries.proposition: Discussion states the expression result and the proposed explanations for lower fragility (shorter transit for RNA polymerase, replication timing) and that replication timing was not measured.
entries.snippet: However, further studies are needed to experimentally determine the effect of intron deletion on replication timing.

entries.proposition: Novelty claim of the authors: first controlled experiment on the function of an extremely large intron.
entries.snippet: This is to our knowledge the first controlled experiment addressing the function of an extremely large intron.

entries.proposition: Intro statement: PRKN loss switches cells to aerobic glycolysis (the Warburg effect), a mitochondrial-theme sentence with no data here.
entries.snippet: its loss has been shown to result in a switch to aerobic glycolysis, known as the Warburg effect

entries.proposition: Supplementary Figure 1C: the 2YFP-tagged PRKN allele remains fragile under aphidicolin (about 24 percent breakage in the tagged cell lines against about 30 percent in wild type), supporting use of the reporter.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Supplementary Figure 1C: bar chart of breakage/constriction at PRKN for four DT40 lines under DMSO or APH with asterisks; APH bars about 24, 47, 18 and 30 percent, DMSO bars about 5 percent.
